entries.title: Overtakes are back, and a pit stop is never one

values.label: the line under his place, the tally, marks on the race bar and the words by his plate as it happens (new)
only the line under his place and the tally

entries.look: Open /live?replay=5542-6759&lap=2 (Monterey Race 1) and let it play at 4×. About four seconds in, Correa passes him: '▽ passed by Correa, lap 2' under P7, the same words above his 9 on the track for a few seconds, a small red mark on the race bar, and '2 passes made, passed twice' below his speed. A minute later Rowe, running second, heads for the pits and drops behind him: the line reads '▲ up 1 as Rowe pitted, lap 3' in grey, nothing by his plate, no mark, and the tally does not move. A pass counts only when Race Control's own pass count agrees; a swap under a yellow, with a car that pits, with a car that stopped, or with three or more cars at once is never one, and the line says what it was. Point at a mark on the race bar to read it; click one to watch it from six seconds before. Sources (top right) has the rule in full. Live uses the same rule; it was not seen live, as no race is running.
